kids.name: value-1
kids.chars: AD-3 (§7 L167, PROPOSED): satisfies if the default-state frames show the mark moving within a still ladder and one re-centre when it reaches the band; violates if the default pins the mark to one row or shows the ladder moving on every update

kids.name: value-2
kids.chars: F-1 (§3 L101, Major): (heuristic) The plan already implies three centring states: the story wants a re-centre "without jitter on every tick", the hotkey line has a resume, and the sign-off checklist names all three. A design that draws one state leaves the other two to the build.

kids.name: value-3
kids.chars: Band rows filled in the 12 px column: the outer 2 rows a side — ILLUSTRATIVE, OQ-3 (E21-D05 #505) owns the edge band, target and minimum interval

kids.name: value-1
kids.chars: AD-4 (§7 L168, PROPOSED): satisfies if a free-scroll frame shows a text state and the resume key, and Space returns to auto-follow; violates if the free-scroll frame is identical to the following frame, or has no resume affordance

kids.name: value-2
kids.chars: F-3 (§3 L103, Major): (heuristic) When a trader scrolls away the ladder must say it has stopped following; a still ladder otherwise reads as a quiet market. 05 §7 also asks for a pause control on any auto-moving content over 5 s, which the free-scroll state serves as.

kids.name: value-3
kids.chars: The state words and the resume key sit in the header area of every free-scroll snapshot; the band column is empty while auto-follow is suspended

kids.name: value-4
kids.chars: Indicator copy is the memo's quote of `14`:1214; E21-D02 #440 writes the header copy

value-1.chars: AD-8 (§7 L172, PROPOSED): satisfies if SCR-051's Ladder tab shows the three options, auto-follow selected, and centre lock carries its every-update-motion caveat; violates if SCR-051 offers a single checkbox, omits a mode, or selects another default

value-2.chars: F-2 (§3 L102, Blocker): (heuristic) A centre lock (the mark pinned to one row) moves every row whenever the price moves. On a click-to-trade grid the row under the pointer then changes between aiming and clicking: a misplaced order, not a slow read.

value-3.chars: The hairline-edged row is the pointer's screen row (board marker); its price changes between aiming and clicking (F-2)
